items.title: Inappropriate to portray pardon power as 'above the law', says Azalina
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: It is inappropriate to portray the exercise of the constitutional power of pardon as an act of being "above the law", said Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. She said the power of pardon was not outside the law, as it is provided for under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution. Azalina, who is also minister in the prime minister's department, said that in respect of offences committed in the Federal Territories, Article 42 provides for the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's power of pardon and establishes the constitutional framework for the Pardons Board.

items.title: Fadhlina: Najib’s conditional royal pardon is King’s prerogative, not Anwar’s or Pakatan’s
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — The decision to grant a conditional pardon to former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak should not be regarded as a decision by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim or Pakatan Harapan, PKR Wanita chief Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said. Fadhlina, who is also Education Minister, said the granting of a pardon is within the jurisdiction of the King as provided for under the Federal Constitution. Fadhlina said the conditional pardon granted to Najib would naturally elicit various reactions, acknowledging the disappointment and anger felt by some quarters.

items.title: Haze: Kuching, Serian among eight areas in Sarawak recording unhealthy air quality
items.summary: In Perak, Seri Manjung recorded an API reading of 164, while Tanjung Malim recorded 118. Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded an API reading of 156, while Cheras recorded 155. Overall, 37 stations recorded moderate API readings, while 10 recorded good air quality.

items.title: Saudi Arabia issues Riyadh air raid alert, explosions heard
items.summary: RIYADH: Explosions were heard in Riyadh on Saturday, an AFP journalists reported, after an air raid alert was issued by Saudi Arabian authorities, regularly targeted in recent days by pro-Iranian Houthis in Yemen. AFP journalists then heard two explosions, and the alert was lifted about half an hour later by Saudi Arabia's civil defence agency. Figures from maritime tracking firm Kpler showed that Saudi exports via the Bab al-Mandab strait had dropped since July, although five loaded ships had passed through in the last week.

items.title: AirAsia 'not too big to fail': Strategist
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Any government assistance for AirAsia Group Bhd should focus on preserving air connectivity, while leaving the airline to resolve its financing needs through private markets, an aviation strategist said. The aviation strategist said excess capacity and fare competition had affected airline profitability in Malaysia and that the country should have managed capacity growth. Then everybody can succeed," he said.

items.title: Viral performance video sparks calls for legal action over alleged insults to Rukun Negara
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) have been urged to conduct an immediate and thorough investigation into a performance video containing elements deemed insulting to the institution of the Malay Rulers, Malaysia and the Rukun Negara. National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said appropriate action should be taken in the event of any violation of the law, with the investigation taking into consideration all relevant and applicable legal provisions, including the Penal Code, Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, Sedition Act 1948 and any other relevant laws. He said such firm action is crucial to serve as a reminder that the freedom enjoyed by every citizen comes with the responsibility to respect the law, national institutions and social harmony.

items.title: #NSTviral: 4am queues as Malaysians rush to get iPhone 18 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: iPhone 18 fever appears to have gripped Malaysians, with some Apple fans reportedly queuing as early as 4am to get their hands on the latest smartphone. Social media posts showed long queues forming at several Apple Store locations across the country today. "TRX, Apple Store at 5.50am," she wrote.

items.title: PMI sees Malaysia as strategic hub
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's advanced manufacturing capabilities, supplier network and talent pool are strengthening its position as a strategic hub for Philip Morris International (PMI), with the company saying the country has an important role to play in its wider Asian operations. PMI East and Southeast Asia and Global Travel Retail president Vassilis Gkatzelis said Malaysia's significance extended beyond its domestic market, with the country supporting the company's global supply chain and exports to about 80 markets. He said PMI viewed Malaysia as a strategic location for advanced manufacturing, talent and supply chain resilience, citing an estimated RM6 billion in export value of PMI devices from the country between 2023 and 2026.

items.title: OpenAI's Sam Altman to brief UNSC as AI safety concerns grow
items.summary: WASHINGTON: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman will brief the United Nations Security Council next week during the annual gathering of world leaders for the UN General Assembly, the company said Friday. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Wednesday called for coordinated international action to address AI risks as fears rise about the dangers of the fast-evolving technology. Concerns about AI safety have escalated in recent weeks, with workers at major AI developers resigning over concerns about the dangers posed by the technology.

items.title: #NSTviral: Man seen trying car doors, entering houses in Setapak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Threads user has claimed that a man who appeared to be jogging tried to open his car door before entering several houses around Persiaran Balau, Setapak. He said the car was locked and its engine was still running, allowing him to drive away after noticing the man's actions. "Luckily, my car was locked and the engine was running, so I drove away," he said.

items.title: Police seek help to locate 18-year-old Qaseh Atika
items.summary: Ampang Jaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Khairul Anuar Khalid said Qaseh Atika Mohd Naim Abdullah's father told police that she had left home and had yet to return. "She was last seen at Jalan UP 3/7B, Taman Ukay Perdana, 68000 Ampang, Selangor," he said in a statement today. Khairul Anuar urged anyone with information on the teenager's whereabouts to go to the nearest police station or contact the Ampang Jaya district police headquarters control centre at 03-4289 7222.

items.title: Nvidia, OpenAI CEOs among tech leaders set for Xi dinner at White House
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Nvidia boss Jensen Huang and OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman are among tech leaders expected to attend a White House state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping next week, a US official said Friday. The AI debate in the US remains dominated by the idea that the country's leading developers – OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta – cannot afford to slow their pace of innovation, whatever the risks, for fear that China will pull ahead. China, long seen as trailing the United States on cutting-edge AI, has been closing that gap fast.

items.title: Trump extends push for US$100,000 H-1B visa fee by another year
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump has extended an executive order that would impose a fee of US$100,000 for H-1B non-immigrant visas by another year, the White House said on Friday. US employers seeking to hire skilled foreign workers can use the federal government's H-1B visa program for a fee, allowing tech and other professionals from abroad to work in the United States for a few years. Trump, who has pursued an aggressive immigration crackdown, has criticized the program and wants to permanently raise the fee from between US$2,000 and US$5,000 to at least US$100,000, though the attempt has faced legal challenges.

items.title: PPP calls for respect for Najib house arrest decision
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The People's Progressive Party (PPP) urged all parties to respect the decision granting former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak conditional house arrest. "The People's Progressive Party calls on all parties to respect and accept the decision of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia," he said in a statement yesterday. It said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, consented to the conditional pardon .

items.title: Woman killed after being run over by trailer
items.summary: ALOR STAR: A cafe worker was killed after she fell from her motorcycle and was run over by a trailer in an accident at a traffic light junction near a shopping mall on Jalan Lencong Barat here yesterday. Kota Setar district police chief Assistant Commissioner Syed Basri Syed Ali said police received a call from a member of the public about the road accident involving the two vehicles. "When they reached the traffic light junction, the traffic light turned green and both vehicles began turning right.

items.title: Drug and scam syndicates busted, goldsmith hit a second time
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Major drug and scam syndicates, a corruption probe involving fertiliser supplies and a massive immigration crackdown were among the cases that kept enforcement agencies busy nationwide over the past week. The period between Sept 11 and Sept 18 saw authorities pursuing more suspects linked to a RM2.4 billion drug laboratory, while Malaysians were arrested in Indonesia over an alleged online scam operation. Meanwhile, hundreds of foreigners were detained during a major multi-agency operation in the heart of Kuala Lumpur, while authorities also moved against syndicates involved in fraudulent immigration documents.

items.title: Trump bans CNN, MS NOW and Politico from White House over 'fake news'
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Friday he was banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, accusing them of spreading "fake news" about his administration. "I am proud to announce that, effective immediately, I am banning Fake News CNN, MSNOW...and Politico...from the White House as a result of their constant 'reporting' FAKE NEWS!" Trump said on his Truth Social platform.

items.title: Trump refuses to rule out demolishing Kennedy Center
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump refused to say whether he would attempt to demolish the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, the iconic facility on Washington's Potomac River. "I think the Trump administration should be recognised as having saved the Kennedy Center because nobody else remembers," Trump said. The Kennedy Center board, which has said the facility requires a US$257 million renovation, earlier this week voted to close the facility for two years for the project.

items.title: Relief for two ex-prime ministers
items.summary: The week was capped by a major legal development involving Datuk Seri Najib Razak, who was granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest. Earlier, former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin was acquitted of four Jana Wibawa-related charges involving RM200 million. Muhyiddin, however, still faces three separate charges in relation to the Jana Wibawa programme.

items.title: Najib's house arrest could revive 'Bossku' sentiment, analysts say [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest arrangement could revive his political influence and inject fresh energy into sections of Umno's grassroots, analysts said. The move could reignite the "Bossku" sentiment and strengthen Najib's role as a symbol and rallying point for traditional supporters, they said, while easing some pressure within Umno over his imprisonment. "The decision gives relief to Najib's supporters and sections of the Umno grassroots.

items.title: US-Greenland security deal to boost Nato, Europe: Danish PM
items.summary: COPENHAGEN: An agreement due to be signed by Denmark and Greenland with the United States giving Washington control over the autonomous Danish territory's security is "good for Nato and Europe," Denmark's prime minister said Friday. Trump said Friday that he had struck an "infinite" deal with Denmark to give the United States control over Greenland's security and bar foreign adversaries from setting up bases there. "I am pleased to announce that the United States of America has entered into an Agreement with The Kingdom of Denmark, and Greenland, that gives the United States permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland," Trump said on his Truth Social network.

items.title: Trump unveils 'infinite' deal for permanent US security control over Greenland
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Friday that he had struck a deal with Denmark to give Washington "permanent control" over Greenland's security that would bar Russia and China from setting up bases in the Arctic territory. "I am pleased to announce that the United States of America has entered into an Agreement with The Kingdom of Denmark, and Greenland, that gives the United States permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland," Trump said on his Truth Social network. Greenland Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen said the deal with the United States "strengthens" the territory's security.

items.title: US court puts brakes on third-country deportations
items.summary: WASHINGTON: A US federal appeals court on Friday broadly upheld a lower court ruling restricting a Trump administration policy of deporting undocumented migrants to countries that are not their own. The three-judge panel of the US Court of Appeals for the First Circuit said people facing "third-country" deportations must be given effective notice ahead of time about where they are being sent to allow them to raise concerns about potential persecution. The Trump administration is expected to appeal the case to the conservative-dominated Supreme Court.

items.title: Nobel Prizes to carry greater cash value this year
items.summary: STOCKHOLM: Winners of the coveted Nobel Prizes will receive more prize money this year after the Nobel Foundation bumped up the award from 11 million Swedish kroner (US$1.12 million) to 12 million (US$1.22 million), reported German Press Agency (dpa). Named after their founder, the Swedish inventor Alfred Nobel, the Nobel Prizes have been awarded annually since 1901 – with few exceptions – in the categories of medicine, physics, chemistry, literature and peace. Sweden's central bank, the Reichsbank, has also established a prize in economic sciences honouring Alfred Nobel.

items.title: Maldives president thanks Malaysia for considering US$100mil currency swap facility
items.summary: HYDERABAD: Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu thanked Malaysia for its decision to consider extending a US$100 million currency swap facility and expressed optimism that bilateral ties would grow stronger following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's recent state visit. "It was an absolute honour to host you, dear Prime Minister @anwaribrahim, on your landmark State Visit to the Maldives. Meanwhile, Muizzu said Anwar's Sept 14-15 state visit to the Maldives "has opened a dynamic new chapter in the enduring bonds of friendship between the Maldives and Malaysia".

items.title: KJ: BN-PH relationship, Anwar-Zahid ties at lowest point
items.summary: Khairy, better known as KJ, said the mood at the 2026 Umno General Assembly reflected growing sentiment among delegates that the party's cooperation with PH had effectively run its course. "That's basically the message from the Umno general assembly," he said in a recent episode of the Keluar Sekejap podcast. However, he said several issues surrounding such cooperation remained unresolved.

items.title: Indonesia recovers 3 more bodies from sunken ship in Java Sea
items.summary: JAKARTA: A joint search and rescue team on Friday recovered three more bodies from a ship that capsized and sank in the Java Sea, bringing the death toll to nine on the sixth day of the search, the Indonesian Navy said, reported Xinhua. Indonesian Navy spokesperson First Admiral Tunggul said naval divers entered the sunken vessel and found the bodies of two men and a woman. Divers also recovered 210 items from inside and around the wreckage, which will be handed over to Indonesia's National Transportation Safety Committee for investigation, said Galih Nurna Putra, commander of the Indonesian Navy base in Banjarmasin.

items.title: Khairy clarifies 'PM-in-waiting' remark on Zahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin has clarified that his description of Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi as a 'prime minister-in-waiting' was not an endorsement of Zahid becoming prime minister. Khairy said his remark was based on his assessment that Zahid had articulated a broader vision for Malaysia, rather than delivering a speech focused solely on party politics. "I said that it was a speech of a prime minister-in-waiting.

items.title: UN holds third informal poll for new chief
items.summary: UNITED NATIONS: The UN's most powerful body, the Security Council, met Friday to again gauge the popularity of contenders to lead the organisation as world leaders prepare to gather for its annual signature event. There is speculation that a compromise candidate could be parachuted into the process at the behest of the powerful five veto-wielding Security Council members – Britain, China, France, Russia and the United States. Each of the 15 Security Council members must anonymously assign each candidate one of three labels: "encourage," "discourage," or "no opinion."

items.title: Norway's King Harald laid to rest in CO2-absorbing sarcophagus
items.summary: OSLO: Norway's King Harald V has been entombed within a ship-shaped sarcophagus carved from a carbon dioxide-absorbing ancient rock, the palace revealed on Friday. A two-person design, the sarcophagus also has space for Harald's widow, Queen Sonja. "The greenish olivine stone can absorb and sequester carbon dioxide, a property that the designers chose as a symbol of King Harald and Queen Sonja's love of nature and their concern for future generations," the palace said.

items.title: KJ: Melaka polls may offer first glimpse of political impact from Najib pardon
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Melaka election could provide an early indication of how the political landscape responds to the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, says Khairy Jamaluddin. Speaking on the latest episode of the Keluar Sekejap podcast, Khairy, better known as KJ, said the election would be the first major electoral development where the political and public reaction to Najib's house arrest could be observed. The former Umno youth chief described the Melaka poll as a potential "first key data point" following the latest development involving Najib.

items.title: Mural of rapper Macklemore painted in Gaza after Sheeran tour furore
items.summary: GAZA/JERUSALEM: Artists in Gaza have painted a mural of Macklemore wrapped in a Palestinian flag on a huge slab of concrete in the ruins of Gaza City, after the US rapper was kicked off Ed Sheeran's upcoming tour for calling for a "Free Palestine". "We wanted to send a message to thank rapper Macklemore in this simple way," said Anne Redwan, 26, who designed and painted the mural with fellow artist Qusai al-Helo. Sheeran said he was unable to keep Macklemore on the tour after stadium owners refused to let him appear.

items.title: Pakatan backs PM’s stance on Najib pardon, says no one is above the law
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) today backed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s stance and the advice given by the Attorney General and Federal Territories Minister to the Pardons Board over former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s conditional royal pardon. In a statement issued after the Pardons Board meeting earlier today, the PH Presidential Council said it firmly stood with the Prime Minister’s position and the advice given to the board. Anwar earlier said the conditional royal pardon did not weaken the government’s resolve to fight corruption.

items.title: Jail and rotan for businessman who tricked director into paying over RM360,000 for AED supply
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — A businessman was sentenced to 14 months’ imprisonment and one stroke of the cane by the Sessions Court here today after pleading guilty to cheating a company director over a project to supply automated external defibrillator (AED) units. Judge Azrul Darus ordered Datuk Seri Azraie Jamaludin, 49, to serve the sentence from today. Azraie, together with another person still at large, was charged with deceiving Lim Wei Xiang, 35, into believing that he had the capacity to secure an AED supply project, which prompted Lim to deposit RM361,150 into the ZAJ Empire Resource bank account belonging to the accused.

items.title: Girl with cerebral palsy in Shah Alam loses RM1m suit over school chair-pulling incident, family to appeal
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 18 — The High Court today dismissed a RM1 million civil suit filed by a teenage girl with cerebral palsy and her parents against six defendants over an incident in which she fell after another pupil allegedly pulled away a chair at a school here in 2023. Judicial Commissioner Datuk Anita Harun also ordered the plaintiffs to pay RM10,000 in costs, national news agency Bernama reported today. Earlier, Federal Senior Counsel Afiq Nazrin Zaharinan, representing all six defendants, sought RM30,000 in costs, while the plaintiffs’ lawyer, Sofian Azmir, sought RM10,000, before the Judicial Commissioner ordered the plaintiffs to pay RM10,000 in costs to all six defendants.

items.title: MCMC steps up social media monitoring as Melaka election preparations gather pace
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 18 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will continue monitoring social media content ahead of the Melaka state election and reminds internet users not to touch on 3R issues involving religion, race and royalty. Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the monitoring was part of MCMC’s role as the regulator of the communications and multimedia sector, with the commission also working with other enforcement agencies when necessary. “MCMC, as the regulator, we will always monitor social media content.

items.title: Nearly 300 higher education sites now connected under nationwide Wi-Fi project
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 19 — The Public Higher Education Institution (IPTA) Wi-Fi project, covering 539 locations nationwide, is expected to be fully completed by September, with 55 per cent, or 294 locations, already having access to Wi-Fi, Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said. She said the project covers 539 locations, involving IPTA and skills training institutions under Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) and the Ministry of Human Resources (Kesuma). Teo said Phases 1 and 2 of the project had been completed at 191 locations, with Phase 3 implementation now underway at institutions under Mara and Kesuma.

items.title: Najib solidarity fund raises RM165,645 in first hour, says Umno sec-gen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Umno’s Najib Razak Solidarity Fund raised RM165,645 within its first hour of being launched today to help former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak pay the RM50 million fine required under his conditional royal pardon, party secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said. “Alhamdulillah, within an hour of its launch, the Najib Razak Solidarity Fund has already reached RM165,645,” he wrote. The fundraising drive was launched after Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi announced today that the party would collect donations to help Najib pay the RM50 million fine.

items.title: Selangor mulls giving free reusable masks to students amid prolonged haze
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Sept 18 — The Selangor state government is considering distributing free reusable cloth face masks to school students as the haze is expected to persist until October. Jamaliah said air quality was expected to improve over the next few days, with Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at moderate or good levels compared with last week. Six areas in Selangor recorded unhealthy API readings this morning, with Johan Setia registering the highest reading at 196, followed by Shah Alam (171), Banting (166), Petaling Jaya (163), Klang (160) and Kuala Selangor (143).

items.title: From 1MDB appeal to billion-dollar civil claims: Najib’s legal battles continue despite conditional pardon
items.summary: The house-arrest arrangement concerns his six-year sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case, involving the misappropriation of RM42 million. The court ordered that the 15-year sentence would commence after Najib completes his sentence in the SRC International case. Najib filed an appeal against the conviction and sentence on December 29, 2025.

items.title: Handful of supporters wait outside Najib’s Langgak Duta residence after conditional pardon
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Around 10 supporters gathered outside former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s private residence in Jalan Langgak Duta this afternoon, following news that he had been granted a conditional royal pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his custodial sentence under house arrest. The group arrived clad mostly in red, with one supporter wearing a red T-shirt featuring Najib’s portrait making a shushing gesture. Earlier today, the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) of the Prime Minister’s Department announced that His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, consented to grant Najib a conditional pardon, permitting him to serve out the rest of his term under home arrest until August 23, 2028, conditional upon the full settlement of an RM50 million fine.

items.title: Gold shop supervisor pawns RM176,200 in gold bars for cryptocurrency, gets 16 months’ jail
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — A former gold shop supervisor who pawned three gold bars to trade in cryptocurrency was sentenced to 16 months' jail and three strokes of the cane by the Sessions Court today for criminal breach of trust. He is also set to be sentenced on a separate criminal breach of trust charge over a pawned gold chain in another Sessions Court. The charges state that Koh, entrusted with three 999 gold bars weighing 50 grammes and 100 grammes, all worth RM176,200, pawned them at a pawnshop for his personal use.

items.title: MCA thanks King over Najib’s pardon, pledges to uphold constitutional supremacy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — MCA has expressed its gratitude to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, for granting a conditional royal pardon to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak. In a statement today, MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong said that honouring the Pardons Board’s decision does not negate the courts' earlier conviction of Najib, just as respecting judicial verdicts does not diminish the King’s constitutional prerogative to grant clemency. “MCA expresses our utmost gratitude for the royal assent granted by His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, regarding the conditional pardon of Former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak,” Wee said.

items.title: Najib’s house arrest: DAP leadership to decide party stance tomorrow, says Loke
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — DAP will convene an emergency central executive committee (CEC) meeting tomorrow to decide its formal position in response to the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, party secretary-general Anthony Loke announced today. Loke noted that the long-term financial fallout remains severe, citing recent Finance Ministry data indicating that 1MDB obligations have saddled taxpayers with RM51.4 billion in liabilities, comprising RM42.5 billion already settled and RM8.9 billion in outstanding debt. Earlier today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim maintained that the pardon does not dilute the government’s resolve to combat graft and power abuse.

items.title: ‘Thank you’: Negeri Sembilan ruler Tuanku Muhriz receives memorandum of loyalty
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Sept 18 — Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir today received a memorandum expressing loyalty and support for him after performing Friday prayers at the Tuanku Munawir Royal Mosque here. Tuanku Muhriz was accompanied by his sons, Tunku Besar of Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-’Abidin. After the prayers, Tuanku Muhriz received the memorandum from Dr Mohd Aluwi Sari, head of the Secretariat for Loyalty and Support for the 11th Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan.

items.title: PAS welcomes Najib house arrest, says he still has plenty to offer
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — PAS today thanked His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, for granting former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak a conditional pardon, saying he could still contribute his ideas and experience to the country. PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the party was grateful for the King’s decision allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to the payment of a RM50 million fine. PAS also prayed that Najib would remain in good health while serving the remainder of his sentence at home.

items.title: Albert Tei fails in bid to move five corruption charges to High Court
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — The High Court today dismissed businessman Albert Tei’s application to transfer five corruption charges against him from the Sessions Court to the High Court. Judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin dismissed the application by Tei, whose real name is Tei Jiann Cheing, 37, on the grounds that the issues raised were not complex and could be adequately dealt with in the Sessions Court. “I do not agree with the applicant’s (Tei) application.

items.title: Anwar: Najib house arrest does not weaken govt’s fight against corruption
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 18 — The conditional pardon allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest does not weaken the government’s resolve to fight corruption and power abuse, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said all corruption cases, including ongoing proceedings involving Najib, must continue in accordance with the law. Anwar said Malaysia must remain firm in tackling corruption, with public support needed to ensure misconduct or abuse of power for personal enrichment is not taken lightly.

items.title: Teen driving Mercedes charged over crash that killed four family members in Kluang
items.summary: KLUANG, Sept 18 — A 19-year-old student pursuing studies in Singapore was charged in the Magistrate’s Court here today with reckless and dangerous driving over a crash that killed four family members last June. Goh Yin Zun pleaded not guilty after the charge was read to him through an interpreter before Magistrate Norasidah A Rahman, Berita Harian reported. Deputy Public Prosecutor Nik Noratini Nik Azam initially proposed bail at RM20,000.

items.title: Press swarm Kajang Prison and Langgak Duta after Najib’s pardon news
items.summary: KAJANG, Sept 18 — Kajang Prison and the residence of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak have become focal points for local and international media following the announcement that he has been granted a conditional pardon by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today. As of 12.30 pm, there was no movement involving the former prime minister detected at the Kajang Prison entrance. Najib, 73, has been serving his prison sentence at Kajang Prison since Aug 23, 2022.

items.title: Zahid announces Umno donation drive to pay Najib’s RM50m fine following conditional pardon
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Umno has launched a nationwide donation drive to assist former party president Datuk Seri Najib Razak in settling the RM50 million fine required under his conditional royal pardon, party president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi announced today. Zahid said the party, representing its entire leadership and grassroots membership, conveyed its profound gratitude to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, describing the royal decision as a moment of tremendous relief for Najib, his family, and party loyalists who had “never ceased to hold hope and offer prayers” for his release. He also called on party members to welcome the royal decision with humility, decorum, and strict adherence to legal norms.

items.title: AGC rejects Zamri Vinoth’s bid to review charge over statement at KL rally
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) has rejected a representation by independent preacher Zamri Vinoth regarding a charge of making a statement likely to cause public alarm in connection with a gathering held in front of a shopping complex in the capital. Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Farhana Mohamad Poad informed Magistrate Faezahnoor Hassan of the decision during proceedings today. Lawyer Nur Shafiqah Shafiyah Omar, representing Zamri, subsequently requested that the court fix dates for the trial.

items.title: Haze update: 35 areas now with ‘Unhealthy’ API, Selangor’s Johan Setia tops 193
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Air quality across Malaysia deteriorated further by midday today, with 35 monitoring stations recording “Unhealthy” Air Pollutant Index (API) levels as of 12pm, according to Department of Environment (DoE) data. Selangor followed closely with six stations recording elevated pollution. Alongside Johan Setia, unhealthy levels were logged in Shah Alam (172), Banting (166), Petaling Jaya (165), Klang (160), and Kuala Selangor (139).

items.title: Hannah Yeoh denies signing Najib house arrest order, calls document fake
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh has denied signing any house arrest order involving former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, which has been circulating on social media. Hannah made the statement in a post on her X account early today. “I have never signed any house arrest order as claimed in the document.

items.title: Najib gets conditional pardon, to serve remainder of sentence under house arrest
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 18 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak has been granted a conditional royal pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest, the Legal Affairs Division announced today. “His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia has consented to grant a conditional pardon to Datuk Seri Najib Razak, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until 23 August 2028, subject to his payment of a fine of RM50 million,” the statement said. The secretariat noted that Najib must strictly comply with all statutory terms attached to the royal pardon.

items.title: Malaysian Armed Forces plans special-needs child centres at major military camps
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) aims to establish at least one Community Rehabilitation Centre (PPDK) at major camps to care for children with special needs. Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the move is part of MAF's efforts to support its personnel, particularly those caring for special needs children. Meanwhile, Malek Razak said MAF is carrying out 898 maintenance projects involving 15,024 units of Armed Forces Family Housing (RKAT) to ensure comfortable living conditions for security force personnel.

items.title: Porsche driver surrenders after driving against traffic to flee Iskandar Puteri roadblock
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Sept 18 — A 43-year-old local man has surrendered to the police after a viral video captured a white Porsche being driven against the flow of traffic to bypass a roadblock in Iskandar Puteri, Johor. In a statement on Thursday, Iskandar Puteri acting police chief Supt Saifullah Jaya @ Yahaya said the district Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division detected the 12-second clip circulating on social media, which showed the sports car being driven recklessly through a police checkpoint at KM6.5 of Jalan Ismail Sultan. The driver turned himself in at the Iskandar Puteri District Police Headquarters on the same day the footage surfaced.

items.title: Officials depart as FT Pardons Board meeting concludes at Istana Negara
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Vehicles carrying Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh and former Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Razarudin Husain were seen departing Istana Negara around 9.40am today following the conclusion of the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting. The impromptu meeting has intensified public speculation that the board convened specifically to deliberate on the royal pardon petition of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, which was deferred during the board's previous sitting on September 11. During that earlier meeting, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, who chairs the board, granted royal pardons to 65 other inmates while Najib's case was held back for further consideration.

items.title: Total standstill on NSE northbound after two box vans overturn near Kuala Kangsar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — A crash involving two box vans that overturned on their sides has completely blocked all northbound lanes of the North-South Expressway (NSE) at KM257.7, along the stretch between the Menora Tunnel and Kuala Kangsar in Perak. The Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) reported that northbound traffic ground to a complete standstill following the incident, triggering a 1.7km congestion queue as of 9.18am. Emergency response teams and recovery machinery are currently on-site working to clear the obstructed lanes.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan’s Yang di-Pertuan Besar greeted by supporters at KLIA
items.summary: SEPANG, Sept 18 — Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir expressed his appreciation for the support shown by over 200 members of non-governmental organisations (NGOs) who gathered at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 here last night to welcome his arrival. Asked if he would immediately resolve the Negeri Sembilan royal institution impasse, Tuanku Muhriz replied briefly: “Yes, insya-Allah , insya-Allah . More than 200 members of Negeri Sembilan non-governmental organisations gather to welcome Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir at Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 1 in Sepang on September 17, 2026.
